title: Data center moratorium approved by Oakland amid AI backlash
key_facts: The Oakland City Council unanimously approved a 45-day moratorium on approvals for new data centres at its Tuesday meeting (6 Oct 2026); the council can extend it.

Councilmember Carroll Fife, who authored the moratorium, says the goal is to give Oakland time to study data centre impacts and change planning and building codes to protect residents' health, safety and welfare.

Oakland has not seen a boom in data centre construction, likely because land and electricity prices are high; a developer has proposed a data centre in a downtown building that used to house a supercomputer.
The Stop AI Data Centers in Alameda County coalition says at least 26 cities in California are considering or have passed similar moratoriums.
San Francisco's Board of Supervisors also approved a 45-day moratorium on data centre approvals on 6 Oct 2026 (the article says 'yesterday').
Mindy Pechenuk, who is running for mayor, urged the council to reject any pause and said she opposes wasting taxpayers' money on a moratorium.
Dohee Kim, an organizer with the Local Clean Energy Alliance, said moratoriums are temporary and that communities need accountability and oversight of AI data centres.
Supporters cite worries about rents, food prices and utility bills; opponents argue data centres will bring jobs and that Oakland needs tech investment.
